newsitem.title: USA: Miami ex-official says innocent in corruption case.
newsitem.headline: Miami ex-official says innocent in corruption case.

text.p: Former Miami City Manager Cesar Odio and a city lobbyist pleaded innocent Wednesday to six counts of conspiracy, embezzlement and witness tampering.
Odio and lobbyist Jorge Luis de Cardenas entered pleas at a brief hearing before U.S. Magistrate Peter Palermo.

A federal grand jury indictment made public Tuesday charged that Odio and de Cardenas conspired with former Miami city manager Manohar Surana to embezzle city money through a contract with a health insurance company. It alleged that they conspired to inflate the monthly insurance bill by $12,500 and divide the extra money among themselves.

The witness tampering charge stems from allegations Odio asked Surana, a native of India, to blame his accented English for a misunderstanding involving the insurance billing amount. Odio's attorney, Richard Sharpstein, said a trial was expected early next year. Odio and de Cardenas remain free on bond.
Sharpstein said Odio never took any city money. He said the money paid to de Cardenas was a legitimate lobbying fee and was paid by the health insurance company, not the city.
If convicted, Odio and de Cardenas face up to 35 years in prison.
Prosecutors said Surana has agreed to plead guilty to unspecified charges and was cooperating with investigators in a probe of public finance corruption in the City of Miami and Dade County.

Former city commissioner Miller Dawkins has pleaded guilty to accepting $75,000 from a computer company seeking a city contract. He is free pending sentencing in January and faces up to 10 years in prison.
